subject: physics
question_text: Define the scalar product of two vectors. Explain the properties of a scalar product with two examples.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The definition
lines: The scalar product of two vectors A and B is
the product of their magnitudes and the
cosine of the angle between them:

lines.text: A · B = A B cos θ

lines: The result is a SCALAR, not a vector.
steps.why: The cosine gives how much of one vector lies along the other, which is why every "along the direction of" quantity turns out to be a dot product.
common_mistakes: Giving the answer a direction; the scalar product has none.

recall.must_convey: That A dot B is A B cos theta and the result is a scalar.

steps.label: The properties

lines.text: A · (B + C) = A · B + A · C

lines: 3) For perpendicular vectors it is zero, and
for parallel vectors it is A B.
steps.why: The zero for perpendicular vectors is the property that gets used most: it is the reason a centripetal force does no work.
common_mistakes: Claiming the scalar product is associative; A · (B · C) has no meaning, since B · C is a scalar.

recall.must_convey: That the scalar product is commutative and distributive, zero for perpendicular vectors and A B for parallel ones.

steps.label: Two examples
lines: Both are scalars built from two vectors.
steps.why: Work is the example the chapter is named for, and it is why the scalar product is introduced here rather than in the vectors chapter.
common_mistakes: Offering torque as an example; torque is a VECTOR product.
Writing the power relation with P on both sides, as P = P · v. Power is the dot product of force and velocity: P = F · v.

recall.must_convey: That work is F dot S and power is F dot v, both scalars.
